title: Equivariant algebra as product of stabilizer fixed rings
statement: Let H and C be commutative rings in one universe with C an H-algebra. Let G be a group and rho:G -> End_H(C) satisfy rho(1)=id and rho(ab)=rho(a) composed with rho(b). Let d be a natural number and alpha:G -> Perm(Fin d) a homomorphism. There exist m <= d and subgroups K(k) of G for k:Fin m such that the equivariant algebra [def-sbc-affine-torsor-equivariant-algebra] is H-algebra isomorphic to the product of the fixed subalgebras C^(K(k)), each defined by the intersection of equalizers of rho(zeta) and id. No geometry, localization, finite-group or domain hypotheses are required.

source.place: Tag 03SF, classification by finite group sets; elementary orbit-stabilizer algebra argument

proof.text: Use the actual orbit quotient of the action alpha, enumerate it by Fin m using Fintype.equivFin, choose Quotient.out as each representative, and define K(k) as its stabilizer. Surjectivity of the quotient map gives m<=d.

Evaluation at representatives lands in the stabilizer fixed rings. To extend a family b, choose t(i) sending the representative of the orbit of i to i, and put f(i)=rho(t(i))(b(orbit(i))). If a and a-prime send the representative to the same point, a-prime inverse times a is in its stabilizer, so the values agree by the action law. This proves equivariance and that extension inverts evaluation. Pointwise operations give an H-algebra homomorphism; AlgEquiv.ofBijective produces the equivalence. The Lean proof is complete and uses only Mathlib.
